settings.heading: Individual Therapy
settings.subheading: One-on-one therapy for adults and adolescents navigating trauma, anxiety, grief, identity, and life transitions. Evidence-based, trauma-based, and tailored to you.

settings.heading: Therapy that takes you seriously.
settings.body:
Individual therapy at Center for Balanced Living begins with a thorough intake process. We want to understand not just your current concerns, but your history, your nervous system, and what you are hoping for.

Sessions are typically 50 minutes and occur weekly or biweekly depending on your goals and scheduling. We offer both in-person sessions at our Townsend, DE office and telehealth sessions throughout Delaware.

Therapy is not a fixed protocol applied uniformly. It is a collaborative process, responsive to what emerges and adjusted as your needs change.

settings.heading: Areas of Care
settings.subheading: We work with adults and adolescents across a wide range of concerns.

settings.title: Trauma and PTSD
settings.description: Complex and single-incident trauma, including childhood adversity, relational trauma, medical trauma, and acute stress responses.

settings.title: Anxiety and Worry
settings.description: Generalized anxiety, panic, social anxiety, OCD-spectrum concerns, and the chronic vigilance that often follows difficult life experiences.

settings.title: Depression and Mood
settings.description: Persistent low mood, anhedonia, bipolar spectrum concerns, and the emotional numbness that can follow prolonged stress or loss.

settings.title: Grief and Loss
settings.description: Bereavement, anticipatory grief, disenfranchised grief, and the complicated mourning that follows traumatic or sudden loss.

settings.title: Identity and Self
settings.description: Questions of identity, belonging, cultural and intergenerational experience, gender, sexuality, and the ongoing work of knowing oneself.

settings.title: Relational Patterns
settings.description: Attachment difficulties, relational trauma, conflict patterns, boundaries, and the ways early experience shapes how we connect with others.

settings.title: Life Transitions
settings.description: Career changes, relationship changes, parenthood, loss of role or identity, and the disorientation of major life shifts.

settings.title: Burnout and Exhaustion
settings.description: Occupational and caregiver burnout, chronic stress, and the depletion that comes from sustained demands without adequate support or recovery.

settings.heading: Evidence-based methods, integrated thoughtfully.
settings.body:
Our clinicians draw from a range of evidence-based approaches, selected based on what fits each client's presentation and goals:

EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) for trauma processing and desensitization of distressing memories.

Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) for anxiety, depression, and patterns of thought that contribute to distress.

Somatic and body-based approaches for clients whose experience of trauma lives in the body and nervous system.

Psychodynamic and relational approaches for exploring how early experience shapes current patterns.

settings.quote: I felt heard from the very first session. For the first time, therapy felt like it was actually built around me.
The work we did helped me understand my patterns instead of just managing them. It changed how I move through the world.
Steady, patient, and never rushed. I always felt like I was in capable hands.

settings.question: Do you accept insurance?
settings.answer: Yes. We accept most major insurance plans including Highmark Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, Cigna, and United Healthcare. We recommend verifying your behavioral health benefits before your first appointment. Our administrative team can help with this process.

settings.question: Do you offer telehealth?
settings.answer: Yes. We offer telehealth sessions throughout the state of Delaware. Telehealth is available for individual therapy and most consultation services. Some evaluation services require in-person attendance.

settings.question: How long does therapy typically last?
settings.answer: This varies considerably depending on your goals and presentation. Some clients find meaningful resolution in 12 to 20 sessions. Others engage in longer-term work spanning a year or more. We revisit goals and progress regularly so that therapy remains purposeful.

settings.question: What is your cancellation policy?
settings.answer: We ask for 24 hours notice for cancellations. Late cancellations and no-shows may be subject to a fee. We understand that life is unpredictable and handle exceptions with flexibility.

settings.question: Are you currently accepting new clients?
settings.answer: Availability varies by clinician. Please reach out through our contact form or call the office to ask about current openings. We do our best to match you with the right clinician based on your needs and preferences.
